findings.summary: two PixelViewport structs, one shadowing the other: the camera stream emitted a double-laned `PixelViewport` into `bbl::upstream` while `bbl::PixelViewport` (int32) already existed, and `resolve_copy_viewport`/`resolve_post_process_viewport` both declare that return type UNQUALIFIED from inside `bbl::upstream` -- so which struct they bind was decided by include order, and only the alphabetical order of the PAL includes kept it working. The emitted struct is gone and the camera resolver returns the existing int32 one, which is what the pin documents and what its two siblings already return; the collision surfaced as a clean compile error the moment the duplicate went. Proved neutral: renderer_plan.cpp byte-identical, scene 73 re-measured 0.003/0.012 on both backends

CameraViewport duplicated NormalizedViewport field-for-field and default-for-default, and its own doc comment named it -- while the SMAA stream emitted the existing one for the same concept in the same wave. Upstream has one type: `resolveCameraViewport` takes `camera?.viewport ?? FULL_VIEWPORT` and FULL_VIEWPORT is a NormalizedViewport. Folded onto it

FULL_VIEWPORT re-typed as four hand-written absent-value strings in the viewport binding; a pinned constant whose second copy would agree only until upstream moved it, and nothing would notice because the lowered resolver would simply resolve a different rectangle. Now read through moduleScopeConstant/propertyInitializer/numericValue, the chain four other lowerers use. Proved neutral: renderer_plan.cpp byte-identical

the camera-viewport [0,1] refusal ran on `staticNumberValue`, which answers undefined for anything it cannot fold -- so refusing only an out-of-range LITERAL let `{ x: t, width: 1 - t }` through with no check at all and would diverge silently outside the unit square, where the pin's inline render-task arithmetic and its clamping exported resolver stop agreeing. A lane this port cannot prove is inside the square now refuses too

nothing kept the physics aggregate's option READERS in step with its table: SHAPE_PARAMETERS drives the struct and the intrinsic, which is a claim about layout, and the five reads in `create_physics_aggregate` were hand-written -- exactly the shape that let `radius` be accepted and silently dropped. A generation-time assertion now checks every lane the table lays into PhysicsAggregateOptions is read as `options.<field>` by the emitted body, the same question `assertShapeParameterMembers` asks from the pin's side

the ~480-line emitted Y-sort module was a MIRROR held by two expression anchors: `keyAt`'s lane and `comesBefore`'s tie were read off the pin, and ensureStorage, syncCount, ensureSorted, the four observers, packRange, uploadSorted, getDrawOrder and the enabler were restated with nothing reading their pinned bodies -- so a bump adding a branch to any of them reorders every Y-sorted layer with generation staying green. Sixteen statement-inventory rows now guard them, measured off the pin rather than guessed, through LoweringContext.assertStatementInventory (the physics lowerer's technique, taken from the shared home rather than a private copy)

the renderable collect arm -- `if ("_gpu" in node && "material" in node) meshes.push(node)`, which is this port's statement of what a renderable IS -- was written character-for-character in two flatten recognizers, with a third and the presence guard asking the same question. Extracted as `provesRenderableCollectArm`, so a pin that renames either field moves one predicate

the composite sub-pass suffix was derived twice with OPPOSITE failure behaviour: `passName` threw on a name that does not start with COMPOSITION_NAME, `inlinePassEffect` silently fell back to the whole name and then reported something misleading -- while three doc comments asserted the identity lived once. Exported `passSuffix` from the module that owns COMPOSITION_NAME; the lowerer adds only its refusal site

the pin-provenance rationale was written five times (parity-scene.ts, capture-instrumented.ts and three tests), and the two shader gates duplicated the guard itself with two different registry lookups. Stated once on `CaptureMeta.pin`, with one exported `captureIsCurrent(sceneId, dir)` both gates call

the CSM aspect was computed per shadow generator from loop-invariant inputs, and my own first fix for it put a function-local `static const CameraRecord` in the loop body -- which emits a thread-safe-init guard on every evaluation. Hoisted beside the `eye` frame constant that already carries the comment saying why, with the default record at file scope

the CSM no-camera arm restated `width / height` where the pinned `effective_aspect_ratio` already answers exactly that for a camera with no viewport -- a second copy of the ratio, one of which is not the pin's. Both arms now go through the pinned body over a default record, whose empty viewport IS the pin's nullish camera

`pack_y_sort_range` -- the innermost loop of the whole Y-sort feature, and the one a full repack runs, which any key change forces -- copied lane by lane through two std::vector<float> subscripts the compiler cannot prove non-aliasing. `std::copy_n` is byte-identical and lowers to a move; the pin writes it lane by lane only because JavaScript has nothing else

`capturePin()` re-read the pin file and re-walked for the repository root on every call, and the staleness check reaches it once per capture directory -- `compose all` and the variant gate both loop over hundreds. Process-cached, like `pinnedLibraryRoot` next door

`run_sprite_renderer_before_update` deep-copied the hook vector on all four frame loops every frame. The copy is what makes it iterate the list it entered with, the way upstream's `for...of` does, so it is kept -- assigned into a retained buffer on the record instead, which pays the allocation once

the coercer-default scan matched ANY two-argument call whose first argument is `config.<x>`, so `Math.max(config.threshold, 0)` would equally be read as a pinned default and first match would decide which. Narrowed to callees declared in the effect's own pinned module. Proved neutral: all 17 of scene 187's composed WGSL modules byte-identical

30 lines of PinnedBinding duplicated verbatim under `camera?.viewport` and `camera?.viewport ?? FULL_VIEWPORT`; bound once under both keys, which also states the real claim -- the two spellings bind identically BECAUSE the members carry the whole-target answers

the same SHAPE_PARAMETERS lane emission rendered twice for the two pinned bags, differing only in the doc prefix, so a change to the lane shape had to land in both. One `shapeParameterLanes(owner)` renders both. Proved neutral: the emitted struct is byte-identical
`PinnedCompositeTask extends PinnedPostProcessTask` re-declared `outputTexture`, which the base already declares non-optionally
`ySortContract` returned a one-field record whose value cannot vary -- `contractError` returns never, so the lane is always 1 after the guard. Returns the number
a doc comment still said `see inlinePass below` after the field was renamed to `inlinePasses`
extract `set_pass_camera_viewport`'s shared half into pal_gpu_shared.hpp, since both PALs write the same early return and resolver call and differ only in the API pair
